The only rated unit, from an Indian programme where villagers actively protect the forest, judges the technology as coping well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5243_2019_forest_fire], which suggests the threat depends on whether fire protection is in place.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__flood.mechanism: Floods drown young plantings: in Australia flooding rains after Cyclone Yasi drowned most saplings in newly planted plots, and a drought year followed by flooding can cause high seedling mortality [ev_flood_hazard_preece23_1, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_3]. WOCAT compilers rate an Ethiopian area closure and assisted natural regeneration in Niger as not coping well with river floods, and the Khost learning site in Afghanistan as not coping well at all with flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1598_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1626_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7460_2024_flash_flood].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__flood.conditionality: The compiler for floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan instead rates it as coping well with river floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1509_2011_general_river_flood]. The WOCAT units are practitioner judgements and the literature units are narrative, so the severity of damage is not quantified; the floodplain system is rated more tolerant than the upland closure and regeneration sheets.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__heat_s.mechanism: On open restoration sites, outplanted seedlings sit in microsites where air at seedling height is 10 °C hotter than at 2 m and soil or litter surfaces up to 30 °C hotter, enough to cause heat stress, and even minutes of extreme heat can kill seedlings of many species [ev_establishment_survival_gross26_2, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__heat_s.conditionality: Both units are review or perspective statements citing other studies, from western North America or unspecified settings, and the perspective piece covers plant restoration generally rather than forests; no unit measures heat-driven mortality at a restoration site in a low-income country.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__landsl.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for assisted natural regeneration in Bangladesh judges it not to cope well with landslides, and the compiler for broadleaf plantations and assisted tree regeneration in India rates it as coping moderately [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4372_2019_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5243_2019_landslide].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__landsl.conditionality: Community reforestation protecting microbasins in Honduras is judged to cope well with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_750_2016_landslide]. These are compiler ratings from a small set of technology sheets, not measurements, and none states how landslides damage the stands.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__sedime.mechanism: Rapid sedimentation and excess leaf litter can cause delayed mortality of mangrove trees by smothering their above-ground aerial roots [ev_establishment_survival_gijsman21_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__sedime.conditionality: This is a single review statement about existing mangrove forests, citing field and laboratory observations, not a measurement on restored stands, and it gives no magnitude.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__waterl.mechanism: In Brazilian restinga, total mortality of planted seedlings over four years did not differ significantly between depressions prone to seasonal flooding (53%) and dry sandbanks (46.5%) [ev_establishment_survival_loureiro21_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__waterl.conditionality: This single site study is the only evidence left in the cell, and it finds periodic waterlogging not necessarily harmful there; it does not quantify losses from longer submergence than the seasonal flooding of those depressions.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__wind_c.mechanism: Wind damages young plantings: on a Spanish dryland project windstorms blew away tree shelters, and strong constant wind in Brazilian restinga breaks branches and damages seedlings [ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1, ev_climate_shock_loureiro21_1]. WOCAT compilers judge afforestation in Cabo Verde as not coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1523_2011_local_windstorm]. In central Vietnam typhoon damage is a continuing concern for smallholder plantations and leads planters to favour short-cycle rotations [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_ieg18_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__wind_c.conditionality: Most other compilers judge restoration technologies in Turkmenistan, Tunisia, Uganda, Niger and Honduras as coping well with windstorms or extratropical cyclones, and reforestation in Honduras as coping moderately with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1529_2012_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_750_2016_tropical_storm]. The WOCAT units are practitioner judgements and the Spanish shelter losses were partly due to poor tethering. The Vietnam evaluation notes that the risk has so far not discouraged smallholders from continuing to plant [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_ieg18_1].

forest_restoration__asset_threat__wind_c.mechanism: On a dryland reforestation project in Valencia, Spain, seedlings lost their tree shelters to windstorms and poor tethering [ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1]. In Florida the 2005 Hurricane Wilma was estimated to have initially destroyed 1250 ha of mangroves, and frequent hurricanes have changed some mangrove ecosystems to mudflats [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__wind_c.conditionality: The Spanish losses were partly due to poor tethering of shelters rather than wind alone [ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1], and the Florida figure concerns existing mangroves and is a cited finding in a review, not a measurement on restored stands [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]. The row rests on two high-income studies, neither of which measures how damage scales with wind speed.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for assisted natural regeneration in Niger judges it to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1626_2014_local_rainstorm].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This rests on a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, not a measurement of storm damage to regenerating stands [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1626_2014_local_rainstorm].

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Niger compiler judges assisted natural regeneration as not coping well with general river floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1626_2014_general_river_flood].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This is a single practitioner judgement from a technology sheet, with no description of the damage and no measurement.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for assisted natural regeneration in Bangladesh judges it not to cope well with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4372_2019_landslide].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This rests on a single compiler rating from a technology sheet; it gives no measure or description of the damage, so it is a compiler rating of how the regenerating stand copes, not a documented failure [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4372_2019_landslide].

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: Compilers in Niger judge assisted natural regeneration as coping well, or moderately on agro-pastoral and pastoral land, with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1626_2014_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_2325_2017_local_windstorm].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: Both units are practitioner judgements from Niger with no description of the damage or measurement.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: Assisted regeneration recovers habitat by letting canopy cover and tree density build up: WOCAT compilers in Bangladesh rate animal and habitat diversity as increased as the habitat improved, and in Niger rate plant diversity as strongly increased where assisted natural regeneration is combined with planting selected species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4372_2019_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2325_2017_plant_diversity]. In Brazilian restinga, artificial perches accelerated the regeneration of native animal-dispersed species, consistent with a cited study in which perches increased seed and seedling abundance and richness [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_2].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: The low-income evidence is compiler ratings without species counts, and the measured evidence comes from a single restoration site in upper-middle-income Brazil using a specific nucleation technique, so transfer to other assisted-regeneration designs is assumed.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in Niger rate assisted natural regeneration as raising above-ground biomass, especially on pastoral and sylvo-pastoral land, and report a rapid increase in soil organic matter; sheets from Niger and Bangladesh also rate soil organic matter as increased [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_2325_2017_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_2325_2017_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_4372_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings with no measured carbon stocks or rates, and soil organic matter enters as a component proxy; the evidence is in context for low-income drylands and Bangladesh but has no measured backing in this row.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The costs are establishment costs per hectare entered by WOCAT compilers for assisted natural regeneration on agro-pastoral and pastoral land in Niger (US$90/ha) and in Bangladesh (US$197.62/ha), plus a table entry of US$639/ha for assisted natural regeneration in Brazil [ev_project_cost_wocat_2325_2017_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_4372_2019_establishment, ev_project_cost_wri17_6].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: The WOCAT values are converted by compilers from local-currency entries, the Brazil table gives no price year, and the Brazil entry is upper-middle income and so outside the low and lower-middle income range; the set is small.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Niger compiler states that assisted natural regeneration on agro-pastoral, sylvo-pastoral and pastoral land, by improving vegetation cover and increasing woody production, helps reduce the impacts of long droughts during the rainy season [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2325_2017_drought_impacts].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: The row rests on a single practitioner rating from a Niger technology sheet, with no measured drought outcome [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2325_2017_drought_impacts].

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Niger compiler reports that by improving vegetation cover and increasing woody production, assisted natural regeneration helps reduce drought impacts [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2325_2017_drought_impacts].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This rests on a single compiler rating from Niger, with no measured drought outcome.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: Compilers for assisted natural regeneration in Niger and Bangladesh rate soil loss and surface runoff as moderately reduced, which is how this row reaches flood [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1626_2014_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4372_2019_surface_runoff].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: No unit rates or measures downstream flooding directly; the link runs only through runoff and erosion proxies. All units are practitioner ratings from technology sheets.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in Niger rate assisted natural regeneration as increasing crop, fodder and livestock production: in the agro-pastoral zone it raised millet and sorghum production in fields, and vegetation cover on sylvo-pastoral land increased by more than 100%, lifting fodder supply [ev_crop_yield_wocat_2325_2017_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_2325_2017_fodder_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_2325_2017_animal_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1626_2014_crop_production].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings from Niger, with no measured yields or comparison plots, and fodder enters as a component proxy for the production gap.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: Recurrent costs are the annual maintenance entered by WOCAT compilers for assisted natural regeneration in Niger (US$108/ha per year) and Bangladesh (US$339.29/ha per year) [ev_project_cost_wocat_2325_2017_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4372_2019_maintenance].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: Both values are converted by compilers from local-currency entries and come from just a pair of technology sheets.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate the long-term returns of assisted natural regeneration as positive or very positive in Niger and Bangladesh, and in Niger report that it contributes to food security and self-sufficiency in the southern regions and lowers the risk of production failure [ev_economic_return_wocat_2325_2017_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_4372_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1626_2014_risk_of_production_failure].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: Every unit is a compiler rating; returns and food security are proxies for poverty, and no unit measures household income or poverty outcomes.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in Niger and Bangladesh rate assisted natural regeneration as reducing surface runoff and soil loss, and the Bangladesh sheet also rates downstream siltation as reduced [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1626_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_4372_2019_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_4372_2019_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings, with runoff and siltation entering as components; no unit measures soil loss.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Bangladesh compiler rates assisted natural regeneration as slightly reducing downstream siltation, the sediment pathway to water quality [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_4372_2019_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This is a single compiler rating, and siltation is a component proxy for water quality.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Niger compiler rates assisted natural regeneration as slightly improving water harvesting and collection [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1626_2014_harvesting_collection_of_water].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This is a single compiler rating without a measured water outcome.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Niger compiler rates assisted natural regeneration as lowering wind velocity, a shelter effect of regenerated woody cover [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1626_2014_wind_velocity].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating of everyday wind speed, not of cyclone or storm damage.

forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.mechanism: Putting tree cover back on cleared or degraded land rebuilds the structure that forest species need, and then lets dispersers do the rest. Measured against degraded ecosystems across 221 study landscapes worldwide, forest restoration enhanced biodiversity by 15-84% and vegetation structure by 36-77% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles16_1]. How the cover is re-established changes the result: natural regeneration surpassed active restoration for plants, birds and invertebrates, with restoration success 34 to 56% higher after controlling for forest cover, precipitation and time [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1]. Recovery is a function of time since disturbance [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1], and the clock is slow — a secondary Atlantic forest was estimated to need 65 years, with a range of 23 to 178, to reach a proportion of 80% animal-dispersed species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2]. What accelerates it is anything that brings seed in or keeps grazing out: beneath framework-species plantings, tree seedlings of many species recruited, 25 of them animal-dispersed and 11 wind-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1]; artificial perches brought native zoochoric regeneration that was absent from the planted rings [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_2]; and Senegalese exclosures carried 27 woody species after a year against 51 in the 5- and 12-year enclosures, more than 52% higher richness [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1]. Practitioners implementing these technologies in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, India, Niger and Turkmenistan record plant, animal and habitat diversity rising as cover returns and protection holds [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4372_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2325_2017_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity]. The other route is keeping the forest that exists, since the governance instruments that retain cover also hold the habitat: GEF sustainable forest management sites lost about 0.27% less forest each year than matched areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1], community forest management in Nepal reduced deforestation [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1], payments improved forest cover and reduced deforestation in pooled analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2], and participatory management is credited with regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2].
forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.conditionality: Planting is not automatically the better route, and in some settings it is the worse one. Where forests can regenerate naturally or with some assistance, reforestation based on tree planting can actually reduce biodiversity conservation benefits if the selected species or management do not provide suitable habitat for species of conservation concern [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1]; plantation after regeneration cutting gave lower species richness than natural regeneration, on very few cases and with a very imprecise estimate [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_1]. Measured against an uncut control forest, plantations lost 40% of local species richness and clear-cut followed by natural regeneration lost 22% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_3]. That comparison is a stand still recovering towards the forest that stood there, which is incomplete recovery against an intact reference rather than damage done by restoration; the gains in this row are measured from cleared, degraded or grazed starting points, and the two baselines must not be mixed. Several outcomes did not move: biodiversity in Vietnamese special-use forests showed no clear-cut evidence of a positive project impact, with the tracking tool judged an unsuitable proxy [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1]; management transfer under Madagascar's Gelose remained superficial and did not stop clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2]; and broadleaf crown-cover change under Van Panchayats was insignificant [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2]. Harm was measured too, though rarely: of 1,924 project locations assessed, 33 (1.7%) showed strong evidence of negative outcomes, all apparently in areas susceptible to urban encroachment, and 169 (8.7%) gave no evidence of a positive outcome [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3]. Two things qualify the strength. Much of the positive weight comes from practitioner ratings on a fixed scale and from forest-cover and governance findings routed in as a component proxy, not from direct biodiversity counts [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. And the benefit is not costless on the farm: a compiler who rated wildlife increasing also recorded that this led to danger of wild life on crops and domestic animals [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity].

forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.mechanism: In low and lower-middle income settings the evidence is mainly WOCAT compiler ratings: area closure in Ethiopia brought back wildlife, assisted natural regeneration in Niger and Bangladesh increased plant, animal and habitat diversity as canopy cover and tree density improved, broadleaf plantations in India provide water and habitat for small animals and birds, and protection measures in Khost, Afghanistan saw migratory animals and birds return [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4372_2019_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_animal_diversity]. Community forest management across community forests in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation, retaining habitat [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1].
forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.conditionality: Management transfers in Madagascar remained superficial and did not stop clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], and the Ethiopian compiler notes that returning wildlife became a danger to crops and domestic animals. No unit in this scope measures species directly: all biodiversity units are compiler ratings and the Nepal and Madagascar units concern forest cover, a component proxy.

forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.mechanism: This row rests on forest-governance evidence pooled across several countries, with forest cover standing in for habitat. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) compared with areas without payments [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]. World Bank participatory forest management projects reported reduced deforestation rates, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity where those outcomes were monitored, and Bank-supported payment schemes had a positive effect on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.conditionality: The payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas, which limits what they deliver for biodiversity [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. Most units measure forest cover or deforestation, a component proxy for biodiversity, not species. The pooled payment effects come from a systematic review and meta-analysis, while the World Bank units are evaluation narratives that cover only projects that monitored outcomes; all concern keeping or managing existing forest through payments or community management rather than restoration planting.

forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.mechanism: In these upper-middle-income settings the evidence is about succession on land that has been cleared or degraded, and about what speeds it up. Tree species richness rose as a function of time since disturbance across an Atlantic rainforest chronosequence [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1], with a forest estimated to need 65 years, range 23 to 178, to reach a proportion of 80% animal-dispersed species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2]. Assisted recruitment shortens the wait: beneath framework-species plantings in Thai dry forest, tree seedlings of many species recruited, 25 of them animal-dispersed and 11 wind-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1], and artificial perches produced native zoochoric regenerants that were absent from planted rings, so bringing in dispersers mattered more than the planting itself [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1]. On Turkmen barkhan sands the revegetated area is recorded as providing habitat for 25-27 species of plants and animals, with plant and animal diversity rated as increasing [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_animal_diversity]. Holding the cover is the companion mechanism: under community forest management in the Sierra Norte de Puebla, forest cover did not decline after the handover but increased by 8% [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1].
forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.conditionality: The direction is consistent, but the base is thin and soft: chronosequences and site studies, a set of compiler ratings, and a forest-cover change read from land-use maps as a proxy for habitat rather than a count of species [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. Where a project was independently evaluated the result was less flattering — biodiversity is hard to assess, the management-effectiveness tool used was not a suitable proxy, and there was no clear-cut evidence that a Vietnamese special-use forest project had a positive impact [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1]. Time is the binding condition: the Atlantic-forest estimate spans decades to well over a century before the assemblage approaches the composition of a mature forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2], so nothing here promises a measurable result inside a project cycle. Two reading rules apply. The gains are measured against the degraded or cleared starting point, not against intact forest, and a young stand holding less than old-growth is incomplete recovery rather than loss. And the perch and framework-species findings are about assisting dispersal into a restoration site [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1]: they presuppose a seed source within reach, which is a siting condition a scan can test and a restoration in a cleared landscape may fail.

forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.mechanism: Restoration accumulates carbon in two pools: biomass as the trees grow, and soil organic carbon after the land-use transition. On biomass, planted forests and woodlots had the highest removal rates at 4.5 to 40.7 t CO2 per hectare per year during the first 20 years of growth, and natural regeneration removed 9.1 to 18.8 [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_3]. Stock estimates line up with those rates: a 20-year-old secondary natural forest in the moist tropical biome was estimated at 51 t of aboveground carbon per hectare [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch19_1], the median present value of 30-year accumulation from natural regeneration is 60.2 tC per hectare in above- and belowground biomass and soil against 44.6 from plantations with cyclical harvest [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_2], and regeneration over 215 Mha could sequester 23.4 Gt of carbon in aboveground biomass over 30 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_williams24_1]. Measured plantings show the accumulation directly: native-species restoration on former pasture held 21.85, 25.78 and 38.29 t C per hectare at three, five and seven years [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_2, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_3], and intervention sites were sequestering approximately 1.33 tons of carbon per hectare per year more than without the project [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1]. On soils, across 151 transitions to forest the average carbon gain was 0.447% of pre-transition soil carbon per year [ev_soil_organic_carbon_busch19_1], afforestation increased soil organic carbon stocks by 26% on croplands [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_1], and practitioners across Niger, India, Tunisia, Uzbekistan, Bangladesh and Eritrea rate soil organic matter and above-ground biomass as rising under these technologies [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_2325_2017_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5243_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1568_2013_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1533_2011_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_4372_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1330_2010_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_2325_2017_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1533_2011_biomass_above_ground_C]. Avoided loss carries the rest: keeping existing cover through community management, payments and project support is counted here as retained carbon [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2].
forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.conditionality: What the land was before, and where it is, decides how much soil carbon is gained — or whether any is. Afforestation raised soil organic carbon by 26% on croplands but by only 3% on pastures and less than 10% on natural grasslands, neither of the latter significantly different from zero [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_3]; in the boreal zone it produced average soil carbon losses of 1.5% against gains of 7% to 17% in other climate zones [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_4, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_5]; clay-rich soils accumulated significantly more while soils lower in clay showed no change [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_6, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_7]; sites with low pre-planting disturbance gained 19% against 4% where disturbance was high [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_9]; and planting density made no difference [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_10]. The biomass figures are growth rates over the first decades, not a permanent stock, and the design choice shows in them: plantations with cyclical harvest store markedly less over 30 years than natural regeneration [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_2, ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_1]. A young restoration is also far from the reference it is growing towards — the same Atlantic-forest study that measured 21.85 to 38.29 t C per hectare in plantings aged three to seven years measured 138.94 in the mature forest [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_3] — which is incomplete recovery against intact forest, while the gain being claimed is against the pasture the planting replaced. Delivery is not guaranteed by the instrument: a REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1], management transfers in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], crown-cover gains in broadleaf forests under community management were insignificant [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], and of 1,924 assessed project locations 33 showed strong evidence of negative outcomes and 169 no evidence of a positive one [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3]. Finally, weigh the mix: the largest totals are modelled potentials over large areas [ev_carbon_sequestration_williams24_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_1], a substantial share of the supporting units are compiler ratings on a fixed scale rather than measurements, the soil meta-analysis is dominated by high-income afforestation rather than tropical restoration [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_1], and forest cover enters as a component proxy for carbon rather than as a stock measurement [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1].

forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.mechanism: In low and lower-middle income settings, WOCAT compilers rate biomass and soil carbon as increased under assisted natural regeneration in Niger and Bangladesh, broadleaf plantations in India, area closure with Acacia reforestation in Tunisia, enclosures with controlled burning in Tanzania, afforestation in Eritrea and Uzbekistan, reforestation in Honduras and protection in Khost, Afghanistan [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_2325_2017_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_5243_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1568_2013_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1607_2014_biomass_above_ground_C]. Community forest management in Nepal retained forest cover by reducing deforestation [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1]. In a systematic review of decentralised forest management, community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points, and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3].
forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.conditionality: No unit in this scope measures carbon stocks or rates: the carbon units are compiler ratings, and forest cover and soil organic matter enter as component proxies. Community management transfers in Madagascar did not stop clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2]. The one unit that measures carbon directly finds no gain: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon in community forests (SMD = 0.09) [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1]. Under Van Panchayats the change in broadleaf crown cover was also insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2]; the Indian, Bolivian and Nepal results are cited in systematic reviews.

forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.mechanism: This row rests on forest-governance evidence pooled across several countries, with forest cover standing in for carbon kept in standing forest. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]. World Bank participatory forest management projects reported reduced deforestation rates and regeneration of degraded forests where those outcomes were monitored, and Bank-supported payment schemes had a positive effect on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.conditionality: No unit measures carbon stocks or sequestration rates: all four measure forest cover or deforestation, a component proxy. The payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. The pooled payment effects come from a systematic review and meta-analysis, the World Bank units are evaluation narratives covering only projects that monitored outcomes, and all concern keeping existing forest through payments or community management rather than restoration.

forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the measured evidence is a native-species restoration on former pasture in Brazil's Atlantic Forest, which held 21.85, 25.78 and 38.29 Mg of carbon per hectare at three, five and seven years [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_2, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_3]. Under community forest management in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla forest cover did not undergo any loss and increased by 8%, which enters here as retained and added cover rather than a carbon stock [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. WOCAT compilers rate above-ground biomass carbon as strongly increased for dune afforestation in Turkmenistan, expecting the numbers to be achieved on the sand dunes in 3 years, and soil organic matter as increased under afforestation in Cabo Verde and in karst areas of Bosnia and Herzegovina [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1529_2012_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1523_2011_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_4367_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C].
forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.conditionality: The same Atlantic-forest study measured 138.94 Mg of carbon per hectare in the mature forest, so the seven-year planting is far from its reference: that is incomplete recovery against intact forest, while the gain claimed is against the pasture the planting replaced [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_3]. The Mexican result is a before-and-after reading of land-use maps with no counterfactual, a proxy for carbon [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1], and the WOCAT units are compiler ratings on a fixed scale rather than measurements.

forest_restoration__catchment_water_yiel.mechanism: This row asks how much water leaves the catchment after forest cover is restored or expanded, and the evidence finds both less and more. Measured syntheses mostly find less: in about 80% of study cases reporting annual water yields the effect of forest restoration and other forms of forest cover expansion was negative, and in 6% positive [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_1]; baseflow decreased in 63% of cases [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_2]; groundwater levels or recharge decreased with forest cover expansion in 67% of the studies reporting them [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_filoso17_1]; no study in the meta-analysis subset showed a water-yield gain [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_3]; and afforesting grasslands reduced annual runoff on average by 44% and shrublands by 31%, with proportionally larger reductions for low flow and 62% at the driest grassland site [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4]. The reason given is interception and use: tropical forest canopies commonly intercept up to 35 per cent of rainfall, and much of the water that soaks in is used by the trees [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1]. On the gain side, baseflow from Ethiopian catchments with exclosures was 1.5 to 4 times greater than from cropland [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1], and a regional land-climate model projects significant increases of 11.4%, 16.9%, 17.6% and 84.9% in four regions under full reforestation potential [ev_water_regulation_teo22_1, ev_water_regulation_teo22_2, ev_water_regulation_teo22_3, ev_water_regulation_teo22_4], while other modelled regions show nonsignificant declines where heightened evapotranspiration outstrips the increase in precipitation [ev_water_regulation_teo22_5].
forest_restoration__catchment_water_yiel.conditionality: What separates the sides is mostly the kind of forest, the baseline and the method. The losses come from plantations and afforestation of grassland and shrubland, measured in paired catchments; reviewers note that most studies referred to plantation forestry rather than restoration with mostly slower-growing native species [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_1], and afforestation is listed as reducing water yield while giving erosion benefits [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_4]. The Ethiopian gain is exclosures compared with cropland, not with unrestored land [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1], and the other gains are modelled, at regional scale, through changes in precipitation as well as evapotranspiration [ev_water_regulation_teo22_1]. Scale also matters: the decrease shrinks at larger temporal and spatial scales [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_3]. Dryness sharpens the loss, which the authors read as more severe effects in drier regions [ev_water_yield_farley05_4]. The actionable distinction is the practice variant: dense plantation planting carries a measured downstream water cost, largest where the catchment is already dry, whereas the gain cases are exclosure on cropland and modelled large-scale reforestation. The gain side is the weaker evidence on catchment yield itself, being one comparison against cropland plus model projections. Groundwater recharge now counts here as a component of catchment yield, and the measured recharge evidence sits on the loss side with the flow records [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_filoso17_1]. A loss here can coexist with the local supply gains practitioners report in the forest restoration water stress row; read the two side by side rather than netting one against the other.

forest_restoration__catchment_water_yiel.mechanism: In the two lower-income contexts in this scope, the evidence reads the other way from the pooled syntheses: baseflow from Ethiopian catchments with exclosures was 1.5 to 4 times greater than baseflow from cropland [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1], and a regional land-climate model projects a significant 84.9% increase in water yield for the Irrawaddy under full reforestation potential by mid-century [ev_water_regulation_teo22_4].
forest_restoration__catchment_water_yiel.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, not whether the restored land itself holds more. Neither unit measures restored forest against the land it replaced: the Ethiopian figure compares exclosure catchments with cropland, and the Irrawaddy figure is a mid-century model scenario at landscape scale, not a project observation. Read it alongside the unscoped catchment water yield row, which pools the wider measured evidence, before treating restoration in a lower-income catchment as a source of extra downstream water.

forest_restoration__catchment_water_yiel.mechanism: Afforesting grasslands and shrublands, mostly with pine and eucalypt plantations in paired catchments, reduced annual runoff on average by 44% and 31% respectively, with proportionally even larger reductions for low flow, and losses far greater at the driest grassland site, at 62% [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4]. Tropical forest canopies commonly intercept up to 35 per cent of rainfall, which evaporates without reaching soil water reserves, and much of the water that does soak in is used by the trees themselves [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].
forest_restoration__catchment_water_yiel.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, not whether the restored land itself holds more. A loss here can coexist with a local gain in the water stress rows, since the trees use much of the water that soaks in [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1]. The evidence is afforestation of grassland and shrubland, mostly in South Africa, Australia and New Zealand, and the authors suggest the effects on water yield will be more severe in drier regions [ev_water_yield_farley05_4]. The FAO–CIFOR synthesis concludes that extensive reforestation or afforestation should not be expected to increase dry-season low flows [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].

forest_restoration__cost_per_hectare_res.mechanism: Cost per hectare depends mainly on method: modelled implementation cost has a median of US$140/ha for natural regeneration against US$3,729/ha for plantations including replanting [ev_project_cost_busch24_1, ev_project_cost_busch24_2], natural regeneration methods are cited at US$12-3,880/ha against US$105-25,830/ha for restoration projects in the tropics and subtropics [ev_project_cost_williams24_2], and natural regeneration in Uganda is tabled at US$26/ha [ev_project_cost_wri17_5]. The opportunity cost of land (median US$4,807/ha) is generally higher and more variable than implementation cost [ev_project_cost_busch24_5].
forest_restoration__cost_per_hectare_res.conditionality: Most reported figures state no price year, some are assumptions (the TEEB study's assumed US$2,390-3,450/ha) rather than observed costs [ev_project_cost_wri17_1], and WOCAT values are compiler-entered conversions from local currency. Values from high-income and upper-middle-income settings are excluded from the low and lower-middle income range.

forest_restoration__cost_per_hectare_res.mechanism: In low and lower-middle income settings, costs are lowest where existing regrowth is used: natural regeneration in Uganda at US$26/ha and assisted natural regeneration in Niger and Bangladesh at US$90/ha and US$197.62/ha [ev_project_cost_wri17_5, ev_project_cost_wocat_2325_2017_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_4372_2019_establishment]. Planting-based work costs more, from rain forest corridor planting in Madagascar (US$938/ha), community forest management in Benin, broadleaf plantations in India and the Khost learning site in Afghanistan to community microbasin reforestation in Honduras at US$5,402.39/ha [ev_project_cost_wri17_4, ev_project_cost_wri17_2, ev_project_cost_wocat_750_2016_establishment].
forest_restoration__cost_per_hectare_res.conditionality: The table and cited values give no price year and the WOCAT values are compiler conversions from local-currency entries.

forest_restoration__cost_per_tco2e_avoid.mechanism: Abatement cost compares implementation and land opportunity costs with the carbon gained: modelled natural regeneration costs a median of US$23.80 per tCO2 and plantations, net of wood-product revenue, US$23.00 per tCO2 [ev_project_cost_busch24_3, ev_project_cost_busch24_4]. In Colombia's western Andes a median carbon price of US$1.99 per tCO2 over 30 years was enough to compensate landowners for letting pastures regenerate [ev_project_cost_chazdon16_1], and conserving 90% of remaining mangroves could be achieved at carbon prices between 3.0 and 13.0 US$ per tCO2 [ev_project_cost_jakovac20_2]. Two payment schemes report low programme costs per tonne of carbon: the PAS scheme in Brazil was estimated at 0.56 USD per ton of CO2, and the Ugandan scheme cost $0.57 per ton of delayed emissions against an estimated social benefit of $1.11 per ton, roughly two times the cost [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_2, ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_3].
forest_restoration__cost_per_tco2e_avoid.conditionality: All units are modelled or break-even prices rather than project budgets, the plantation range runs from negative (profitable without carbon payments) to US$724 per tCO2, and the mangrove conservation figure concerns avoided emissions from protecting existing forest rather than restoration; the Colombian figure is cited from another study and states no price year. The Brazilian figure is a total programme cost given without assessing cost-effectiveness, both payment figures are cited in a systematic review, and both concern paying landholders to keep existing forest rather than restoring it [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_2, ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_3].

forest_restoration__cost_reduction.mechanism: Natural regeneration lowers cost by letting forests grow back on their own or with low-cost assistance, cited at US$12-3,880/ha against US$105-25,830/ha for restoration projects, and is often more effective than full tree planting in long-term success [ev_project_cost_williams24_1]; European guidelines likewise note its lower cost and locally adapted genetic material [ev_project_cost_stanturf26_1]. In a mulching experiment in tropical dry deciduous forest on Mexico's Jalisco coast, polyethylene mulch cut the cost of each established plant, including nursery costs, from 18.00 USD on bare soil to 2.45 USD, because 92 of 180 plants established against 10 of 180 without mulch [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]. Decentralised administration of Van Panchayat forests in India is associated with costs approximately 1/13th of those under state administration [ev_project_cost_samii14_1].
forest_restoration__cost_reduction.conditionality: The European statement is an expert assertion that also notes limits in species composition, and the cost comparison is a cited range without price year. Organic mulches cut cost per established plant less, to 12.50 USD with alfalfa straw and 13.33 USD with leaf litter, and the result comes from a single experiment at one site [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]; the Van Panchayat cost figure is cited in a systematic review and concerns administering existing forest [ev_project_cost_samii14_1].

forest_restoration__cost_reduction__inco.mechanism: Measures taken at planting can cut the cost of each tree that survives. In a Mexican tropical dry forest, polyethylene mulch raised establishment from 10 of 180 unmulched plants to 92 of 180 and brought the cost per established plant down from USD 18.00 to USD 2.45, nursery costs included; alfalfa straw and leaf litter cost more material and established fewer plants, at USD 12.50 and USD 13.33 per plant [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]. At the other end of the scale, a successful black-mangrove project in Tabasco reforested 50 ha at USD 3,945.60 per hectare, a figure that covers sanitation, dredging, soil conservation works, ridge restoration, training, plant production, transplanting and monitoring [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_2].
forest_restoration__cost_reduction__inco.conditionality: The two figures are not comparable and neither is a cost saving on its own: the mulch result is a cost per surviving plant from a single trial on three species, while the mangrove figure is a whole-project cost per hectare for one site, reported in a diagnostic study without a comparison against a cheaper alternative [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1, ev_project_cost_hernmel17_2]. Both come from Mexico, an upper-middle-income setting, so they say little about what the same works would cost elsewhere, and the mangrove cost is a second-hand figure attributed to a local project record [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_2].

forest_restoration__cross_family__biodiv.mechanism: A global meta-analysis of 221 study landscapes found that forest restoration enhances biodiversity by 15 to 84% and vegetation structure by 36 to 77% compared with degraded ecosystems, as regrowing forest rebuilds habitat structure [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles16_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__biodiv.conditionality: This rests on a single meta-analysis in which restored sites are secondary or selectively logged forests and active and passive restoration are not separated, so it cannot attribute the gain to a particular restoration family.

forest_restoration__cross_family__catchm.mechanism: A global systematic review pooling forest restoration with forestry and afforestation found that annual water yield decreased in about 80% of study cases reporting it and increased in 6% [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_1], baseflow decreased in 63% of cases [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_2], groundwater levels or recharge decreased in 67% of the studies reporting them [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_filoso17_1], and no water-yield gains were observed in the meta-analysed subset [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_3]. Tropical forest canopies commonly intercept up to 35 per cent of rainfall, which evaporates without reaching soil water reserves, and much of the water that does soak in is used by the trees themselves [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__catchm.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, with groundwater recharge counted as a component, not whether the restored land itself holds more. Local supply sits in the water stress rows, and a loss here can coexist with a gain there, since the trees use much of the water that soaks in [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1]. The decrease shrinks at larger temporal and spatial scales [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_3]; the review reports vote counts rather than pooled sizes, is dominated by temperate and Oceania studies, and the baseflow cases are few [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_2].

forest_restoration__cross_family__cost_p.mechanism: Across restoration families, the opportunity cost of land is generally higher and more variable than implementation cost, with a modelled median of US$4,807/ha [ev_project_cost_busch24_5]; restoration projects in the tropics and subtropics are cited at US$105-25,830/ha [ev_project_cost_williams24_2] and the TEEB study assumed US$2,390-3,450/ha [ev_project_cost_wri17_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__cost_p.conditionality: These are modelled, cited or assumed values rather than observed project costs, none states a price year, and they pool restoration methods without separating families.

forest_restoration__cross_family__drough.mechanism: A meta-analysis of catchment restoration in Ethiopia reports that exclosures, tree planting, bunds and terraces reduce water losses and improve the quantity and quality of water in soils, rivers and aquifers, a pathway to drought resilience [ev_soil_water_retention_meaza22_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__drough.conditionality: This is a single source on soil and stream water, a component of drought impact rather than a drought outcome, and it pools exclosure and planting with soil and water conservation structures, so the share due to tree restoration is not isolated [ev_soil_water_retention_meaza22_1].

forest_restoration__cross_family__flood_.mechanism: This row rests on a single global systematic review: flooding or peak flows decreased with forest cover expansion in 82% of the studies with data on them, consistent with forest cover slowing storm runoff [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__flood_.conditionality: The review pools explicit and implicit forest restoration with forestry and afforestation, is dominated by temperate and Oceania studies, and reports vote counts rather than effect sizes, so it does not say how large the reduction is or which restoration practice delivers it [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1]. No unit comes from a low- or lower-middle-income setting. Expert positions point the other way: an FAO–CIFOR synthesis concludes that massive forestation programmes proclaimed as the answer to preventing floods simply will not do the job, although reforestation may bring other benefits [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_3], and a published comment argues that reforestation does not necessarily reduce flooding if soil properties do not recover, river bed morphology does not change and settlements, roads and drains remain [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_5]. Neither is a measurement.

forest_restoration__cross_family__flood_.mechanism: This row rests on a single global systematic review: flooding or peak flows decreased with forest cover expansion in 82% of the studies with data on them, consistent with forest cover slowing storm runoff [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__flood_.conditionality: The review pools explicit and implicit forest restoration with forestry and afforestation, is dominated by temperate and Oceania studies, and reports vote counts rather than effect sizes, so it does not say how large the reduction is or which restoration practice delivers it [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1]. No unit comes from a low- or lower-middle-income setting. Expert positions point the other way: an FAO–CIFOR synthesis concludes that massive forestation programmes proclaimed as the answer to preventing floods simply will not do the job, although reforestation may bring other benefits [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_3], and a published comment argues that reforestation does not necessarily reduce flooding if soil properties do not recover, river bed morphology does not change and settlements, roads and drains remain [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_5]. Neither is a measurement.

forest_restoration__cross_family__heat_s.mechanism: Satellite comparisons of forest gain and loss show that more forest cools the land surface locally in tropical and temperate regions, with the largest cooling where tropical forest cover rose by about 50%, while forest loss warms it [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_4, ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_5].
forest_restoration__cross_family__heat_s.conditionality: The cooling is absent in boreal regions [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_3]. The evidence is a single global remote-sensing study of observed forest-cover change, not of planting or regeneration as such, and land surface temperature is only a proxy for heat stress.

forest_restoration__cross_family__heat_s.mechanism: Gaining forest cover cools the land surface: forestation lowered annual land surface temperature by 0.18 degC in the tropics and 0.19 degC in temperate regions, and forestation of about 50% in tropical regions led to cooling of 1.11 degC, while deforestation warmed the tropics by 0.38 degC [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_4, ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_5].
forest_restoration__cross_family__heat_s.conditionality: Boreal regions showed a null effect [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_3]. The source is a single remote-sensing study of observed forest-cover change rather than a named restoration practice, it measures annual land surface temperature rather than heat extremes, and microclimate buffering enters as a component of heat-stress hazard.

forest_restoration__cross_family__produc.mechanism: Under the Reflorestar payment programme in Espírito Santo, Brazil, the poorest quarter of municipalities saw agricultural value added rise by 8% and the value of agricultural production by about 14% [ev_agricultural_production_value_seixas24_2, ev_agricultural_production_value_seixas24_3].
forest_restoration__cross_family__produc.conditionality: The gain holds only for the poorest municipalities; the better-off municipalities showed a 14% decline, and aggregate municipal indicators showed no significant effect. The programme pools standing-forest conservation with regeneration, planting, agroforestry and silvopasture, and municipal production value is a proxy for the farm production gap in an upper-middle income setting.

forest_restoration__cross_family__rural_.mechanism: Restored forests can diversify livelihoods and raise income from timber and non-timber forest products [ev_household_income_iufro20_8]; in Wuqi County, China, the sloping land conservation programme increased local incomes by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times [ev_household_income_wri17_1], and global estimates put the benefit-cost ratio of restoring degraded forest land at 7.5 to 30.9, including public goods [ev_economic_return_wri17_1, ev_economic_return_wri17_2]. A meta-analysis of payment-for-environmental-services programmes finds a positive effect on overall household income (SMD = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__rural_.conditionality: Restoration can also take agricultural land and reduce on-farm income or employment [ev_household_income_iufro20_7], few studies conclusively show that restored-forest benefits alleviate poverty, which occurs over years or decades when it does [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_4], and Brazil's Reflorestar programme showed no significant effect on municipal GDP, value added or employment [ev_economic_return_seixas24_1]. The Wuqi gain is ex post without a counterfactual and largely off-farm and subsidy-driven, the benefit-cost ratios are global model estimates, and income and returns are proxies for poverty. The same meta-analysis finds no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11), on nonagricultural income or on household assets [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2], so the income gain does not show up as farm income or wealth.

forest_restoration__cross_family__soil_e.mechanism: Tree roots stabilise slopes: forests lower the probability of shallow landslides, and landslides increase as roots decay about three years after clearance, remaining high until regenerating roots mature at around 15 years [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_7, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_2]. After clear-felling in Alaska, USA, the landslide-affected area was 5 times greater than before logging, and mass erosion on steep terrain can rise two- to more than ten-fold after harvesting [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_3, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4].
forest_restoration__cross_family__soil_e.conditionality: During extreme rainfall, very weak slopes or seismic activity, and for deep-seated failures, forest cover is unlikely to have any effect [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_8]. The evidence describes forest loss rather than restoration, comes mostly from temperate and high-income settings, is recorded under erosion for lack of a landslide category, and rests on a single FAO review citing other studies and expert consensus.

forest_restoration__cross_family__water_.mechanism: Expanding forest cover moves water in two opposite directions within the same review. More water gets into the soil: in 83% of the studies reporting on infiltration capacity or soil infiltration, infiltration increased [ev_soil_permeability_filoso17_1]. Less reaches groundwater: in 67% of the studies with data on groundwater levels or recharge, groundwater decreased with forest cover expansion [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_filoso17_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__water_.conditionality: The two sides are measuring different things, soil infiltration and groundwater, and the evidence does not say which drives water stress for a given user. A farmer depending on soil moisture and a household depending on wells or springs fed by recharge would read them differently; the groundwater decrease is a measured harm for the latter. Timing also separates them: aboveground benefits recover within a few years, but infiltration and recharge are counted in decades rather than years [ev_soil_permeability_iufro18_1], an expert panel conclusion rather than a measurement. A French review citing a global analysis reports species richness losses after clear-cutting followed by natural regeneration relative to uncut forest, though smaller than under plantations [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_3], the meta-analysis compares regeneration with planting rather than with degraded land [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1], and the Ethiopian compiler notes that returning wildlife damages crops and livestock [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity]. The Senegal result compares exclosures of different ages at one site rather than exclosures with open grazed land [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1].

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Secondary forests regrowing on abandoned farmland and pasture accumulate carbon in biomass and soil: global reviews give CO2 removal rates for natural regeneration in its first 20 years, Brazilian Amazon and Atlantic Forest regrowth approaches mature-forest biomass over decades, Colombian regenerating forests reached about half of old-growth carbon stocks, and soil carbon recovers within years and rises after transition to forest. WOCAT compilers in Tanzania and Tunisia rate biomass carbon and soil organic matter as increased and emissions as decreased, citing controlled bush fire.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: Most of the evidence is pantropical modelling and chronosequences in upper-middle-income Brazil and Colombia; above-ground biomass takes decades to approach old-growth values, and the Amazon figure is biomass rather than carbon from slash-and-burn fallows. The global potential estimates assume regrowing forests are allowed to persist, and the Tanzanian and Tunisian entries are compiler ratings.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: In Ethiopia, catchments under exclosure pass more baseflow downstream than cropland does: baseflow from catchments with exclosures was 1.5 to 4 times greater than the baseflow from cropland [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, not whether the restored land itself holds more. It rests on a single meta-analysis from a single country, and the comparison is with cropland rather than with unrestored degraded land, so the size is a contrast with farmed land, not a measured restoration gain. It runs against the measured syntheses on planted forest in the other catchment water yield rows; whether regeneration behaves differently from planting in this respect is suggested here, not shown.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Natural regeneration is cheap to implement because it relies on regrowth rather than planting: a model across low- and middle-income countries gives a low median implementation cost, and a WRI table of African restoration costs lists natural regeneration in Uganda at a low per-hectare cost.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The model cost is time-discounted over a fixed horizon and restricted to land near natural forest, and the Uganda figure is a single table entry with no price year; only the Uganda figure enters the class, and neither includes the opportunity cost of land.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Because natural regeneration has low implementation cost and accumulates carbon, a global model finds a moderate median abatement cost per tonne of CO2 once implementation and opportunity costs are included, and a Colombian study cites a low carbon price sufficient to compensate landowners for letting pastures regenerate.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: Both are modelled or break-even prices rather than observed project costs: the global estimate is limited to land near natural forest and discounted, and the Colombian figure is cited second-hand from an upper-middle-income Andean setting.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Natural regeneration lowers restoration cost compared with planting where forests can grow back on their own or with low-cost assistance, as stated by a pantropical review and by IUFRO restoration guidelines that also cite locally adapted genetic material.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: These are statements of relative cost from a review and expert guidelines (the latter set in Europe), not measured comparisons, and the guidelines note limits in the species composition that regeneration delivers.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures achieved crop yields 188 to 222 kg/ha higher than households beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a panel estimate put the advantage at 586.6 kg/ha of grain after controlling for soil fertility, labour, fertilizer and other factors [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The benefit was more pronounced in the drier first year, shown by a significant negative interaction between land management and year [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3]. All units come from one study of exclosures compared with open grazing in a low-income, semi-arid mixed crop-livestock setting, and the yields are those of downstream cropland rather than of the restored area.

In Tanzania, the compiler for riverine area enclosures rates bush-fire hazard as reduced, and attributes the reduction to the enclosure itself, fire breaks and local bylaws [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1607_2014_fire_risk]. In Ethiopia, the compiler for an area closure on degraded land rates fire risk as slightly increased, without giving a reason [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1598_2014_fire_risk].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: What separates the two ratings, as far as the sources say, is fire management: the reduction is credited to fire breaks and bylaws added to the enclosure [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1607_2014_fire_risk], while the Ethiopian closure names no such measures [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1598_2014_fire_risk]. A design implication follows for scoping: pair a closure with fire breaks and enforced bylaws rather than relying on the closure alone. Neither side is stronger than the other; both are single compiler ratings with no measured fire incidence, and the Ethiopian rating states no mechanism, so the idea that recovering vegetation adds fuel is an inference, not a finding.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Compilers judge that closing degraded hillsides and other degraded land in Ethiopia to let vegetation recover reduces downstream flooding, most rating the reduction strong and one noting that runoff from the watershed is highly reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_flooding].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings from Ethiopian area-closure sheets, not measurements, so the row speaks to a single country and practice. One closure on degraded lands rates the downstream benefit only slight [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1598_2014_downstream_flooding].

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for regeneration-based technologies in Ethiopia rate downstream flooding as reduced, one explaining that runoff from the treated watershed is highly reduced as vegetation recovers.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings from Ethiopian WOCAT sheets in a low-income setting, with no measured discharge or flood data, so the strength of the effect rests on practitioner judgement.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Tanzania and Tunisia report that regenerating enclosed areas mainly raise fodder production, harvested as cut-and-carry grass that in turn supports animal production; some also rate crop production as increased, citing deeper, more fertile soils and mulch made available from the area. forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: One Ethiopian compiler rates crop production as unchanged, and the compiler-rated gains run mainly through fodder, a component of the production gap rather than crop yield; apart from the Tigray study, all units are compiler ratings, not measurements. forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The Tunisian compiler rates farm income as decreased and long-term maintenance returns as neutral, even while rating food self-sufficiency as improved. Almost all units are WOCAT compiler ratings, poverty is reached only through income, return and food-security proxies, and the literature units are cited examples or general review statements rather than measured income effects.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Recovering vegetation cover slows runoff and holds soil: WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Tanzania and Tunisia rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, attributing it to improved vegetation cover, controlled runoff and sediment deposited behind bunds, with one Ethiopian compiler noting soil loss halved within the first years. forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The same global assessment reports that abandoned terraced land is particularly prone to gully erosion and landslides, and one Ethiopian compiler rates downstream siltation as worse. Apart from that assessment and the Ethiopian meta-analysis, which measures runoff as a component of erosion, all units are compiler ratings, and some regeneration sheets combine enclosure with physical structures such as bunds, so the share due to regrowth alone is not isolated [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1].

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for regeneration-based technologies in Ethiopia and Tanzania rate downstream siltation as decreased, citing less sediment transported, improved vegetation cover with controlled erosion, and sediment trapped behind bunds; reduced sediment load is the component of water quality this row rests on.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: One Ethiopian compiler rates downstream siltation as increased. All units are compiler ratings of siltation used as a component proxy, with no measured water-quality data, and some sheets combine enclosure with bunds.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate water quantity and the harvesting or collection of water as improved under area enclosure in Tanzania and area closure with Acacia reforestation in Tunisia, the Tanzanian compiler attributing it to a reduction in unproductive loss of both green and blue water [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1607_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1568_2013_harvesting_collection_of_water].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: An Ethiopian compiler rates water quantity as unchanged under area closure on degraded lands [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1598_2014_water_quantity]. The pool is a handful of compiler ratings with no measured flow, soil-moisture or groundwater data. Water leaving the catchment for downstream users is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Compilers rate excess-water drainage in both directions. For one Ethiopian area closure and for closure with acacia reforestation in Tunisia, drainage is rated as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_excess_water_drainage]; for another Ethiopian area closure it is rated as slightly worsened [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_excess_water_drainage]. None of the three ratings states a mechanism.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The sources give nothing that separates the two sides: no site, soil or design detail is attached to any rating. One visible difference is that the Tunisian technology includes planting acacia, whereas both Ethiopian ratings, one on each side, are for closure alone [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_excess_water_drainage]. All three are practitioner ratings with no measured drainage, so this row records a disagreement among compilers rather than a tested effect.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: The compiler for an Ethiopian area closure rates wind velocity as strongly reduced as vegetation recovers on the closed land [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1414_2011_wind_velocity].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating of everyday wind speed; it says nothing about cyclone or storm damage to people or to the regenerating stand.

forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.mechanism: On a Mediterranean dryland reforestation project in Spain, the drought index correlated strongly with the course of plantation mortality (r = −0.72); about one quarter of the plantation was dead by the first year and more than half in the second, and the trend worsened in an exceptional, severe drought [ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_1, ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_2].
forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.conditionality: All three units come from one study in a high-income dryland, so agreement cannot be judged and the strength is not quantified. The authors add that an extreme drought can reveal, several years later, the impact of inappropriate technical measures that would otherwise remain concealed, so the losses mix drought with planting technique [ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_3]. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.conditionality: A single compiler rating, below the evidence floor, not a measurement of storm damage to plantings. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.mechanism: In central Vietnam typhoon damage is a continuing concern for smallholder plantations and leads planters to favour short-cycle rotations [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_ieg18_1]; on a Spanish dryland reforestation project, windstorms blew away tree shelters [ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1].
