Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__biodiver.mechanism: These are plantation-versus-natural-regeneration comparisons from an INRAE expert synthesis focused on temperate and boreal forests. Its own small meta-analysis of species richness in plantations against natural regeneration of the stand after regeneration cutting gives -0.24, a very imprecise estimate from a very small number of cases whose interval spans zero [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_1]. The synthesis also reports that plantations generally lead to decreases in biodiversity, or at least to changes in composition at the expense of native species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_6], and cites a 40% loss of local species richness in forest plantations relative to uncut control forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_2].
forest_restoration__plantation__biodiver.conditionality: The no-effect class comes from the imprecise meta-analytic estimate alone. The decline statements compare plantations with uncut or near-natural forest rather than with the land a plantation replaces, so they are held out of the class as reference shortfalls [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_6]; every unit in this row nonetheless points toward loss, none toward gain. Read the class as no demonstrated difference from natural regeneration in a very small sample, not as evidence that plantations are neutral for biodiversity. All of it is temperate and boreal evidence, outside the target. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__carbon_s.mechanism: A global review finds planted forests and woodlots have the highest CO2 removal rates, 4.5 to 40.7 t CO2/ha/yr during the first 20 years of growth [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_1], and plantation reforestation with cyclical harvest accumulates a modelled median of 44.6 tC/ha across aboveground and belowground biomass, soil and harvested wood products [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_2]. Soil carbon also rises: afforestation of cropland raised soil organic carbon stocks by 26% on average and tropical transitions to plantation gained 0.919% of pre-transition soil carbon per year [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_busch19_2], and the compiler for afforestation of degraded irrigated cropland in Uzbekistan reports surface biomass growth of 20 t/hectare/year and soil organic matter up by 20% in the form of fallen leaves [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1533_2011_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1533_2011_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C].
forest_restoration__plantation__carbon_s.conditionality: Soil gains are conditional: on pastures (3%) and natural grasslands the change was not significantly different from zero, boreal sites lost 1.5% while other zones gained 7 to 17%, low-clay soils showed no change, heavily disturbed site preparation cut the gain to 4% against 19% with low disturbance, and plantation density made no difference [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_4, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_9, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_10]; that meta-analysis draws mostly on high-income temperate sites. The planted-forest removal range spans eucalyptus, teak and pine among other species, and the modelled 44.6 tC/ha counts harvested wood products and is a discounted present value [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_2]. These are production-plantation results, planted forests, woodlots and plantations under cyclical harvest. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__catchmen.mechanism: Afforesting grasslands and shrublands reduced annual runoff on average by 44% and 31%, with proportionally larger reductions for low flow and losses of 62% at the driest grassland site [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4]. A cited review of forestation effects on streamflow found that most studies reported decreases in water yields, and that most of those studies referred to plantation forestry rather than forest restoration with mostly slower growing native species [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_1].
forest_restoration__plantation__catchmen.conditionality: These are afforestation and plantation-forestry results from paired catchments, mostly in South Africa, Australia and New Zealand; the authors suggest the effects on water yield will be more severe in drier regions [ev_water_yield_farley05_4]. Forest plantations of native tree species aged 25 to 45 years produce persistent dry-season streamflow deficits exceeding 50% relative to native old-growth forests, because of high water use by young, densely-spaced trees [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_3]; that comparison is against old-growth forest rather than the land the plantation replaced, so it is held out of the class as a reference shortfall. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__cost_per.mechanism: In a plantation trial on pasture in La Chontalpa, Tabasco, Mexico, semi-mechanised planting cost US$178/ha against US$217/ha by hand [ev_project_cost_keyes97_1, ev_project_cost_keyes97_2]; plantation establishment in the Masoala corridors of Madagascar is listed at 279 dollars per hectare [ev_project_cost_wri17_3]; and modelled implementation cost for plantations across low- and middle-income countries has a median of US$3,729/ha, inclusive of replanting after harvest cycles, against US$140/ha for natural regeneration [ev_project_cost_busch24_2].
forest_restoration__plantation__cost_per.conditionality: The cost class is set by the Madagascar entry, the only one in the low-income band; the Mexican and modelled figures sit outside it. The Mexican figures are historical field costs for establishment and first-year maintenance that exclude donated seedlings, and the modelled median counts replanting over harvest cycles, with an interdecile range of US$1,530–11,675/ha [ev_project_cost_busch24_2]. These are production-plantation costs, not the cost of restoration toward a natural baseline. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__cost_per.mechanism: Modelled across areas feasible for plantation in low- and middle-income countries, the abatement cost of climate mitigation through plantation, accounting for revenue from the sale of harvested wood products, has a median of US$23.00 per tCO2, with an interdecile range of US$−14.80 to 724 [ev_project_cost_busch24_4].
forest_restoration__plantation__cost_per.conditionality: A single modelled source, below the evidence floor, so it is described here but does not set a class; the figure nets out wood-product revenue from harvest, which is why its range reaches below zero. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__fire__al.mechanism: The compiler for afforestation and tree planting in Uganda rates fire risk as unchanged so far, but notes that with dense forest comes the risk of fire, which is common in a neighbouring district though not yet a problem locally [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_fire_risk].
forest_restoration__plantation__fire__al.conditionality: A single compiler rating from a technology sheet, below the evidence floor, so it is described here but does not set a class; it is a warning that fire risk may rise as the stand closes, not evidence that planting reduces fire. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__flood__a.mechanism: The compiler for afforestation and tree planting in Uganda rates downstream flooding as reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_flooding].
forest_restoration__plantation__flood__a.conditionality: A single compiler rating from a technology sheet, below the evidence floor, so it is described here but does not set a class; it is a judgement, not a measured flood record. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__flood_ha.conditionality: A single compiler rating from a technology sheet, below the evidence floor, so it is described here but does not set a class. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__rural_po.mechanism: In Vietnam smallholder plantations were a sound investment, with an economic rate of return of 13.2 percent at completion and substantial financial gains for participants, mainly because low-interest loans reduced up-front costs to near zero [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1]. In Guanacaste, Costa Rica, payments for environmental services under the reforestation modality made up 18.66% of participants' income during the contract, covered a substantial part of the costs of establishing and maintaining the plantation, and brought family employment and legal security over the property [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3]; similar Latin American programmes reach around 10% of family income [ev_household_income_padilla17_2]. Modelled plantations would be profitable even without carbon payments across 28.3% of the area feasible for them [ev_economic_return_busch24_1], and compilers for afforestation in Uganda and Uzbekistan rate long-term returns as very positive, the Uzbek compiler noting that unprofitable land would start bringing benefit [ev_household_income_wocat_1533_2011_farm_income].
forest_restoration__plantation__rural_po.conditionality: These are production-plantation results: smallholder plantations, commercial plantations under a payment scheme, and modelled plantations with harvest. The Vietnam return fell short of the 17.0 percent expected at appraisal and the gains depended on subsidised loans [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1], the Costa Rica evidence comes from a high-income setting, and the Uganda compiler rates farm income as unchanged [ev_household_income_wocat_1577_2013_farm_income]. Most units are compiler ratings or modelled, and income and returns are proxies for poverty. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__soil_ero.mechanism: Both directions are reported. Under good tree cover erosion falls: in eucalyptus afforestation in Calabria, Italy, sediment concentrations were substantially greater on a plot with little or no tree cover, confirming the importance of the forest canopy in reducing erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1], and the Uganda afforestation compiler rates soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as reduced [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1577_2013_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_siltation]. On the loss side, forest plantations without understory can increase the kinetic energy of throughfall beyond that of rainfall and increase detachment of soil particles [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_2], and particularly serious erosion problems arise in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3].
forest_restoration__plantation__soil_ero.conditionality: What separates the two sides is the ground layer under the trees: the gains come where canopy and cover are good, the losses where understorey and litter are absent or removed [ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1, ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_2, ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3]. The actionable reading is a management condition, keeping understorey and litter, rather than a property of plantations as such. The loss side is cited statements from syntheses rather than measurements, and the gain side is a high-income Italian catchment study plus compiler ratings. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__water_qu.conditionality: A single compiler rating, below the evidence floor; siltation is a component proxy and no unit measures water quality directly. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__waterlog.mechanism: In Uzbekistan, the compiler for afforestation to rehabilitate degraded irrigated cropland rates excess-water drainage as improved at +3, through bio drainage through transpiration [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1533_2011_excess_water_drainage]; the Uganda afforestation compiler rates drainage as unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_excess_water_drainage].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__bio.mechanism: Protection and community forest management retain and expand forest habitat. GEF sustainable forest management projects show less deforestation than matched areas without projects [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management in Nepal reduced deforestation [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1], and forest cover increased by 8% under community management in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate plant and animal diversity as increased under protection [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_plant_diversity]. Forest governance instruments retain forest habitat: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]. World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1], and in Bolivia four payment-like initiatives showed marked environmental protection effects, two intermediate and three weak [ev_biodiversity_outcome_robertson05_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__bio.conditionality: Most units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction, a component proxy for biodiversity, and the Mexican figure is a before-after comparison with no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. In south-west Madagascar transfers of management to communities were found superficial and unable to stop forest clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], and GEF project sites likely exposed to urban encroachment showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3]; the GEF evidence concerns existing forest under a bundle of protection and management rather than restoration. Governance effects are uneven: under Van Panchayats the change in broadleaf crown cover was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], an evaluation of Vietnam's special-use forests found no clear-cut evidence that the project had a positive impact on biodiversity, noting that its tracking tool was not a suitable proxy [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. These governance units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction rather than species, the Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in a systematic review, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cat.mechanism: Standing forest passes a smaller share of its rainfall to streams than other land cover: globally, the mean water transmission fraction is 33.8% for forests against 40.8% for non-forests [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_2], and replacing forest cover with other land uses almost always results in increased runoff and streamflow [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_2].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cat.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, not whether the restored land itself holds more. Keeping forest standing therefore means less water downstream than clearing it would, and this can coexist with the local gains recorded in the protection water stress row. Both units compare existing forest with other land cover; neither measures the outcome of a protection or community forest management project, and the transmission difference may not hold locally [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_2].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.mechanism: Costs cover establishing community-managed forest and protection works: compiler-entered establishment costs on WOCAT sheets for an afforested community forest with plantation and fodder nursery in India and for a protected area in Afghanistan, and a WRI table entry for community management of forest resources with sustainable fuelwood production in Benin.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__rur.mechanism: Protection and community forest management can reduce poverty through forest income, employment and food from forests. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2], 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases [ev_household_income_iufro20_1], and community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards [ev_household_income_iufro20_2]. Exposure to standing forest feeds children: high forest exposure gives at least 25% greater dietary diversity in sub-Saharan Africa [ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_1, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_2, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_3, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_4], child dietary diversity rises with community tree cover across 21 African countries, and in Malawi children in communities that experienced deforestation had less diverse diets [ev_food_security_iufro15_2, ev_food_security_iufro15_1]. In a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent and by 66% for low-income households, consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management raised participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, poorer households compensated for lost land access gained 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. In Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_household_income_ceballos21_1], households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_household_income_gefieo19_1], in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1], non-timber income rose after benefit-sharing at Bach Ma, Vietnam [ev_household_income_ieg18_3], and WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate food self-sufficiency and long-term returns as improved [ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_economic_return_wocat_5243_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_7460_2024_costbenefit_maintenance_long].

In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; the GEF forest-management portfolio has a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 [ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, local studies found no effect of REDD+ on material well-being, and an analysis in Indonesia found potentially negative effects [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6]; payment programmes have a small positive or neutral effect on poverty [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3], and payments had no significant effect on a food consumption index in Mexico [ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1], where the payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2]. Benefits skew to the better-off: in Nepal poor and low-caste households receive much less while bearing more costs [ev_household_income_iufro20_3]; near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests forest income rose by an insignificant 2 per cent and lowest-quartile households lost 6 per cent and 10 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; at Bach Ma benefits were shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. Livelihood components often fail: just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their livelihood aims, and benefit-sharing around Vietnam's special-use forests averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact [ev_household_income_ieg13_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_2]. Protected-area gains depend on tourism: no child growth or wealth gains were found near protected areas without documented tourism [ev_food_security_naidoo19_2], and the forest-diet effect turns significantly negative in richer communities [ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_5]. The protected-area, tree-cover and forest-exposure studies measure what living near standing forest provides, not the outcome of a restoration intervention; the Colombian benefit of $411–1,236 per hectare a year is a carbon valuation, not cash income [ev_economic_return_wri17_3]; and many figures are secondary citations in reviews or World Bank evaluation estimates without a comparison group.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__soi.mechanism: This row describes the slope stability that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. Land managers and scientists agree that forests lower the probability of shallow landslides, and to a lesser extent deep-seated movements, in upland areas [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_7]. Clearing removes that protection: landslides begin to increase when roots decay at around three years after forest clearance and susceptibility remains high until around 15 years, rates of mass erosion on steep forested terrain can rise two- to more than ten-fold 3-15 years after timber harvesting, and in southeast Alaska the area affected by landslides after logging was 5 times greater than in a 100-year period before it [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_2, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_3]. WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, the Indian compiler noting that trees and other vegetation helped slow down sediment and runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7460_2024_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis likewise notes that landslips may occur due to the loss of forest cover, tree roots giving the soil a certain amount of mechanical support, and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes reported by participatory forest management projects where monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__soi.conditionality: The role of forests for deep-seated landslides is considerably less, and during extreme events with copious rainfall, very weak slopes or seismic activity forest cover is unlikely to have any effect [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_8]. The landslide units are forest-loss contrasts and expert consensus, largely from temperate regions and cited second-hand, so they show what clearing costs rather than measuring the outcome of a protection or community forestry programme [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_2, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_3, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4]. The India and Afghanistan units are compiler ratings from sheets that bundle several practices. The root support is limited to shallow (<1m) mass movements, and deep-seated (>3m) landslides are not noticeably influenced by the presence or absence of a well-developed forest cover [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_2]. A measured governance result is null: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.mechanism: The Indian Van Panchayat WOCAT compiler rates downstream siltation as decreased because vegetation helped slow down sediment and runoff, the component of water quality this row rests on.
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.conditionality: A single compiler rating of siltation used as a component proxy; there are no measured water-quality data.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate water quantity, availability and harvesting or collection as improved: the Indian compiler cites better soil water-holding capacity from slower runoff and improved spring discharge in the peak dry season, and the Afghan compiler cites water seeping into the ground through revegetation and improved land cover, recharging the water table [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_harvesting_collection_of_water].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.conditionality: The units are compiler ratings from sheets that bundle several practices — broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries in India, a learning site for sustainable land and forest management in Afghanistan — with no measured flow or groundwater data, so the gain cannot be credited to protection alone. Whether keeping forest standing changes the water passed downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__win.mechanism: The India compiler rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as strongly reduced, explaining that erosion from extreme rain storms is reduced by decreasing flow velocity [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__win.conditionality: This single practitioner rating describes rain-storm erosion, not wind damage, so it is weak support for a wind or cyclone effect. The programme bundles plantations, assisted regeneration and nurseries with village protection.

forest_restoration__recurrent_cost.mechanism: Recurrent costs are annual maintenance costs per hectare entered on WOCAT sheets for regeneration, community forest and other restoration technologies in Niger, Bangladesh, India, Afghanistan, Honduras and Bosnia and Herzegovina [ev_project_cost_wocat_2325_2017_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_750_2016_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4367_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4372_2019_maintenance], plus a WRI table entry for eucalyptus and native-species reforestation in Brazil [ev_project_cost_wri17_11]. A payment scheme in Costa Rica is estimated to spend between $255 and $382 per year per hectare of additional forest [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].
forest_restoration__recurrent_cost.conditionality: Values span a very wide range because the technologies and cost items differ, the WOCAT figures are compiler entries mostly converted from local currency, and the WRI figure has no price year [ev_project_cost_wri17_11]; the units from upper-middle-income countries were set aside from the class, which rests on the low- and lower-middle-income entries. The Costa Rican figure is a payment for keeping forest, expressed per hectare of forest that would not otherwise have been there, and is cited in a systematic review rather than drawn from programme accounts [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].

forest_restoration__rural_poverty.mechanism: Restoration reaches poverty mainly through income from forest products, payments and employment. Restored forests contribute to diversified livelihoods and higher income from timber and non-timber products, naturally regenerating forests supply both, and secondary forest regeneration combined with palm-fruit harvest in Brazil's Atlantic forest improved farmer income [ev_household_income_iufro20_8, ev_household_income_chazdon16_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_10]. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests, 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases, community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards, and in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]. In China, the Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, and afforestation subsidies raised off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9]; in Costa Rica, payments for reforestation made up 18.66% of participants' income, against about 10% of family income in other Latin American programmes [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_2]. Global modelling gives benefit-cost ratios of $7.5 to $30.9 for restoring 350 million hectares of degraded forest land and about $2 to $32 across forest biomes, and plantations would be profitable without carbon payments across 28.3% of the plantation-feasible area [ev_economic_return_wri17_1, ev_economic_return_wri17_2, ev_economic_return_busch24_1]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand, and households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. WOCAT compilers across Africa, Asia, Central Asia and Latin America mostly rate long-term returns as positive or very positive and food self-sufficiency or production risk as improved; the Niger compiler estimates that assisted natural regeneration raises food security by 20% at least, and the Indian compiler cites more fodder and water [ev_economic_return_wocat_1048_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1577_2013_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1533_2011_farm_income]. Forest governance and payment programmes add measured income effects. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services finds a positive effect on overall household income (SMD = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent on average and by 66% for low-income households, per capita consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, 72 percent of wage jobs went to the poorest and poorer households compensated for lost land access gained an income increment of 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. In Vietnam smallholder plantations were a sound investment, with an economic rate of return of 13.2 percent at completion and substantial financial gains, mainly because low-interest loans reduced up-front costs to near zero [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1]; restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; China's Sloping Land Conversion programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]; and in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty.conditionality: Negative and null findings are substantial. Reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection without viable alternatives, and restoration can reduce on-farm income by taking agricultural land [ev_household_income_le12_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_7]; the Turkmen compiler expects annual income to fall by 20 - 25% for the first 1-2 years, the Tunisian compiler rates farm income as reduced, the Ugandan compiler rates it unchanged, and the Cabo Verde compiler rates food security unchanged because the practice reduces land-use options [ev_household_income_wocat_1529_2012_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1568_2013_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1577_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and the Gelose transfers did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, other REDD+ studies found no effect or potentially negative effects in Indonesia, and payment programmes have either a small positive or neutral effect on poverty [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3]. Brazil's Reflorestar programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment, the GEF forest-management portfolio returns a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 counting carbon only, and in Nepal benefits of community forestry go mostly to better-off households while poor households bear more of the costs [ev_economic_return_seixas24_1, ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. Few studies have substantiated that services of restored forests alleviate poverty, and where they do it takes years or decades [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_4]. Much of the positive evidence is WOCAT compiler ratings, carbon valuations rather than cash (such as $411–1,236 per hectare a year for forest conservation in Colombia), perception scores (the Costa Rica economic impact of 63.9%), secondary citations, or subsidy-driven gains without a counterfactual (Wuqi) [ev_economic_return_wri17_3, ev_household_income_padilla17_3, ev_household_income_wri17_1], and protected areas, REDD+ and payment schemes are conservation instruments rather than restoration practices. The newer governance evidence carries its own nulls and losses: payments had no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11) or on a food consumption index in Mexico (0.09 SMD) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2, ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1]; forest income near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests rose by an insignificant 2 per cent, and households in the lowest income quartile saw forest incomes reduced by 6 per cent and 10 per cent, the gains being concentrated among wealthier households [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]; and around Vietnam's special-use forests benefit-sharing averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact on livelihoods, while at Bach Ma non-timber income rose but was shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_2, ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. Vietnam's plantation return fell short of the 17.0 percent expected at appraisal and its gains rested on subsidised loans [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1], Mexico's payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2], and the Amazon returns are modelled. The decentralised-management and payment figures are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank income figures are evaluation estimates, the Andhra Pradesh one measured against project start-up rather than a comparison group.

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: In the high-income contexts the evidence is about payments for reforestation in north-west Costa Rica. Payments for environmental services represent 18.66% of participants' economy relative to their other income during the contract period, and the programme's overall economic impact scored 63.9%, mainly by covering a substantial part of the costs producers incur in establishing and maintaining the plantation, with family employment and legal security over the property the main perceived benefits [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: This is a small base from one survey of participants: the income share is a share of income during the contract, not a change against non-participants, and the impact score is a perception index rather than measured welfare [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3]. The plantations are commercial reforestation under contract, so the gain rests on the payments, and the benefits declined for later contract cohorts as payments were not updated while labour and transaction costs rose. The mangrove cost comparison in this row is not a household benefit and does not set the direction: mangrove restoration projects reported a median cost of US$0.1 per square metre (range 0.05–6.43) and an average replacement cost ratio of 5 (95% CI 3.1–6.9) against breakwaters giving the same wave reduction, a saving in engineering cost that accrues to society [ev_frmg_nara16_3].

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: Restoration and community forest management reach poor households mainly through income, food and fodder. In a rigorous analysis of 18,000 community forests in Nepal, community forest management reduced both poverty and deforestation; community forest management in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on household living standards, particularly for those closer to forests and with more education; and household survey data around GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. The benefits of mangrove reforestation projects were found to outweigh their costs in the Philippines, and a World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD per hectare [ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1, ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. WOCAT compilers in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Honduras, India, Niger, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Uganda and Uzbekistan rate long-term returns on establishment and maintenance costs as positive or very positive [ev_economic_return_wocat_1048_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1330_2010_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1533_2011_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1577_2013_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1607_2014_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_7460_2024_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_750_2016_costbenefit_establishment_long], and most rate farm income, food self-sufficiency or production risk as improved: the Niger compiler estimates that assisted natural regeneration raises food security by 20% at least and reduces forage deficits so livestock keepers are not forced to sell their animals in the lean season, the Indian compiler cites more fodder and water, and the Ethiopian and Uzbek compilers cite sales of grass and wood and unprofitable land starting to bring benefit [ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1533_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1330_2010_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1626_2014_risk_of_production_failure].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: Gains are uneven and sometimes absent. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable for lack of valid alternatives, and the Gelose transfers raised neither community incomes nor the money usable in the area [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]. REDD+ contributions to household income in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, and studies of community forest management in Nepal find poor and low caste households receive much less than well-off households while bearing more of the costs through patrol labour and grazing controls [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. The Tunisian compiler rates farm income as reduced and maintenance returns as neutral, and the Ugandan compiler rates farm income as unchanged [ev_household_income_wocat_1568_2013_farm_income, ev_economic_return_wocat_1568_2013_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_household_income_wocat_1577_2013_farm_income]. Most units are WOCAT compiler judgements on technology sheets rather than household measurements; the Nepal, Madagascar living-standards and Philippines findings are secondary citations in reviews; the Uganda result compares household assets near and far from project sites; and the Bangladesh figures are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression in grey literature [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1, ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. Community forest management and REDD+ are forest governance instruments rather than restoration practices, and apart from the Nepal poverty analysis every unit measures income, returns or food security as a proxy for poverty.

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: Payments for environmental services raise household income on average: a meta-analysis of payment programmes in low- and middle-income countries finds a positive effect on overall household income (standardised mean difference [SMD] = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: The gain does not come from farming: the same meta-analysis finds no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11, 95% CI [−0.06, 0.29]), on income from nonagricultural sources (0.05 SMD) or on household assets (SMD = 0.04) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2]. Livelihood components of conservation projects often fail: just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]. The row rests on a single systematic review with meta-analysis and a single portfolio evaluation; income is a proxy for poverty, and both concern payment and protection programmes for existing forest rather than restoration.

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings income gains come from subsidies, payments, forest products and plantation finance. China's Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, afforestation subsidies increased off-farm labour earnings, and the programme's benefits exceeded its costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9, ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]. Community forestry in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]; secondary forest regeneration coupled with palm-fruit harvest improved farmer income in Brazil's Atlantic forest [ev_household_income_iufro20_10]; restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually [ev_household_income_ieg13_2]; and in Vietnam smallholder plantations were a sound investment, with an economic rate of return of 13.2 percent at completion and substantial financial gains for participating smallholders [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1], payments reach around 10% of family income in other Latin American programmes [ev_household_income_padilla17_2], and WOCAT compilers in Cape Verde, Turkmenistan and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate long-term returns as positive [ev_economic_return_wocat_1523_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1529_2012_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_4367_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: Null and negative findings sit alongside the gains. The Turkmen compiler expects annual farm income to fall by 20 - 25% for the first 1-2 years, the Cape Verde compiler rates food security unchanged, REDD+ sites in Indonesia showed potentially negative effects on well-being, and Brazil's Reflorestar payments programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment [ev_household_income_wocat_1529_2012_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_economic_return_seixas24_1]. In Mexico payments had no significant effect on a food consumption index (0.09 SMD) and the PSAH scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1, ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2]. Around Vietnam's special-use forests benefit-sharing averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact on livelihoods, while at Bach Ma non-timber income rose but was shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_2, ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. Vietnam's plantation return fell short of the 17.0 percent expected at appraisal, and the smallholder gains rested on low-interest loans that reduced up-front costs to near zero [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1]. The Chinese gains are subsidy-driven and the Wuqi figure has no counterfactual, the Colombian figure is a carbon valuation rather than cash income [ev_economic_return_wri17_3], the Amazon returns are modelled, and the payment and benefit-cost figures are cited in systematic reviews.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk.mechanism: Tree cover reduces erosion by protecting the soil surface, slowing runoff and holding slopes. In the Potwar Upland of Pakistan runoff and sedimentation from sheet erosion fell 55 percent and 78 percent five years after tree planting and closure of slopes to grazing [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5, ev_runoff_reduction_forbes11_1]; in Ethiopia, a meta-analysis finds areas closed to grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites, and tree planting on degraded catchments cut annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. Targeted reforestation of 9.3 percent of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment is modelled to decrease landslide sediment inputs by about 20 percent, tree planting on susceptible slopes can reduce landslide risk, eucalyptus afforestation plots in Calabria, Italy with good canopy gave lower sediment concentrations than plots with little or no tree cover, and China's reforestation programmes reduced soil erosion and sediments [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_1, ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1, ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_1]. WOCAT compilers across Africa and Asia widely rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased under planting, regeneration and area closure, citing vegetation cover, sediment held upstream and slower flows [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. A World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes participatory forest management projects reported where they were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk.conditionality: Forest plantations without understory can increase the kinetic energy of throughfall and soil detachment, and abandoned terraced land can be particularly prone to gully erosion and landslides [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_2, ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_4]; an Ethiopian area-closure compiler rates downstream siltation as worse [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation], and afforestation in New Zealand reduces erosion at the cost of water yield [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3]. The Pakistan result combines planting with grazing exclusion, most units are WOCAT compiler ratings, several sheets bundle planting with structures such as bunds or terraces, the measured plot and model evidence is mostly from high-income temperate settings, and the runoff results (including the Ethiopian runoff coefficients) measure a component of erosion risk rather than soil loss [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1]. Management matters: an FAO–CIFOR synthesis warns of particularly serious erosion in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3]. Governance alone may not show up on the ground: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1], cited in a systematic review.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: In high-income temperate settings tree cover reduces erosion through canopy protection and slope reinforcement: eucalyptus afforestation plots in Calabria, Italy with good canopy gave lower sediment concentrations than plots with little or no tree cover, confirming the importance of the forest canopy in reducing erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1]; reforestation of just 9.3 percent (159 km2) of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment could decrease total landslide sediment inputs by about 20 percent [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6]; afforestation in New Zealand provides erosion reduction benefits [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3]; and reforestation in Slovakia's Hornad watershed is modelled to decrease surface runoff [ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: The New Zealand afforestation benefit comes with reduced water yield [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3], the Waipaoa and Hornad results are model scenarios, and the Italian evidence compares well- and poorly-covered plots within an afforested catchment rather than afforested against unplanted land [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6, ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1]. The row applies only to high-income contexts and does not transfer directly to low-income settings.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings, planting, area closure and regeneration reduce runoff and the soil it carries. In the Potwar Upland of Pakistan runoff and sedimentation from sheet erosion fell 55 percent and 78 percent five years after tree planting and closure of slopes to grazing [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5, ev_runoff_reduction_forbes11_1]; in Ethiopia, a meta-analysis finds areas closed to grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites, and tree planting on degraded catchments reduced annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Eritrea, Uganda, Tanzania, Niger, Tunisia, India, Bangladesh, Tajikistan and Afghanistan rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1607_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1626_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_4372_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_soil_loss]: an Ethiopian compiler reports an initial 50% reduction in soil loss after 2–3 years, the Tanzanian compiler controlled soil erosion through vegetation cover, and the Indian compiler says trees and other vegetation helped mitigate displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: An Ethiopian area-closure compiler rates downstream siltation as worse, and the Tajikistan compiler rates only a slight decrease in soil loss [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_soil_loss]. Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings rather than measurements, some sheets bundle planting with structures (an Ethiopian compiler attributes reduced siltation to sediments deposited behind the bund), and the Pakistan result combines planting with grazing exclusion [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5]. The Ethiopian meta-analysis values are runoff coefficients and depths, a component of erosion risk rather than measured soil loss [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. One measured governance result is null: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1], cited in a systematic review.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: World Bank projects using participatory forest management reported reduced soil erosion among their environmental outcomes, where those outcomes were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1]. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis reports the opposite in a particular setting: particularly serious erosion in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard, or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: The two sources are separated by management of the ground layer, which is a design choice: the erosion problem is tied to stripping vegetation and litter beneath plantations [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3], whereas the reduction is reported for participatory management of forests [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1]. For scoping, the sentence that matters is to keep understorey and litter in place; trees alone do not protect the soil. Neither side is strong: one is a portfolio evaluation narrative without magnitudes that covers only projects that monitored the outcome, with possible positive-reporting bias, and the other is a cited general statement about plantations; neither measures soil loss.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: China's national reforestation and afforestation programmes increased forest cover with reduced soil erosion and sediment, and WOCAT compilers in Cape Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate soil loss, runoff and downstream siltation as decreased.
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: The Chinese finding is a narrative summary of programme outcomes without an effect size, and the other units are compiler ratings; this row applies only to upper-middle-income contexts.

forest_restoration__water_quality_risk.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for planting, regeneration and protection technologies in Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, Cape Verde, India and Bangladesh rate downstream siltation as decreased, citing less sediment transported, sediment trapped behind bunds, improved vegetation cover and slower runoff; lower sediment load is the component of water quality this row rests on.
forest_restoration__water_quality_risk.conditionality: One Ethiopian compiler rates downstream siltation as increased. All units are compiler ratings of siltation used as a component proxy, with no measured water-quality data, and some sheets combine vegetation with physical structures such as bunds.

forest_restoration__water_stress.mechanism: This row is about water on and under the restored land: springs, soil water and dry-season supply for the people who use them. Practitioners applying these technologies rate water quantity, availability and the harvesting of water as improved, one recording improved spring discharge in the peak dry season, another that the technologies improve the water-holding capacity of the soil by decreasing runoff velocity, another a reduction in unproductive loss of both green and blue water, and another that through revegetation and improved land cover water seeps into the ground, recharging the water table [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1607_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1626_2014_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1568_2013_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1523_2011_water_availability].
forest_restoration__water_stress.conditionality: Read this row as local supply. Measured groundwater-recharge evidence, which found recharge decreasing with forest cover expansion, now sits in the catchment water yield rows; check wells and springs that depend on recharge there before assuming a gain. Timing matters: compilers in Honduras and Ethiopia rated water quantity unchanged, the Honduran compiler noting that effects of reforestation will show in the long term [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_750_2016_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1598_2014_water_quantity]. All of the positive weight is practitioner rating from technology sheets, several of which bundle more than one practice, rather than measured flow or soil moisture. What restoration does to the water leaving the catchment for downstream users is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

forest_restoration__water_stress__income.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings the positive evidence rests on infiltration and baseflow. In Ethiopia a meta-analysis found baseflow from catchments with exclosures 1.5 to 4 times greater than from cropland [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1], and a land-climate model projects a significant increase in water yield of 84.9% in the Irrawaddy basin under full reforestation [ev_water_regulation_teo22_4]. WOCAT compilers in India, Afghanistan, Tanzania, Tunisia and Niger rate water quantity, availability or harvesting as improved [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1607_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1568_2013_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1626_2014_harvesting_collection_of_water]: the Indian compiler says the technologies improve the water holding capacity of the soil by decreasing runoff velocity and cites improved spring discharge in the peak dry season, the Afghan compiler that through revegetation water seeps into the ground, recharging the water table, and the Tanzanian compiler a reduction in unproductive loss of both green and blue water.
forest_restoration__water_stress__income.conditionality: Compilers for area closure in Ethiopia and reforestation in Honduras rate water quantity unchanged, the Honduras compiler expecting effects of reforestation only in the long term [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1598_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_750_2016_water_quantity]. Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings rather than flow measurements, several from sheets that bundle planting with other practices; the Ethiopian baseflow result compares exclosure catchments with cropland rather than with the degraded land before restoration [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1]; and the Irrawaddy gain is a model projection at basin scale [ev_water_regulation_teo22_4]. This scope holds no measured catchment evidence of the water-yield losses that afforestation causes elsewhere.

forest_restoration__water_stress__income.mechanism: A global synthesis of paired catchments found that afforestation reduced annual runoff on average by 44% when grasslands and 31% when shrublands were afforested, with proportional reductions even larger for low flow and losses of 62% at the driest grassland site, suggesting more severe effects in drier regions [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4]. Trees use the water: tropical forest canopies commonly intercept up to 35 per cent of rainfall, which evaporates without reaching soil water reserves, and trees use much of the water that does soak in, so extensive reforestation or afforestation should not be expected to increase dry-season low flows [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].
forest_restoration__water_stress__income.conditionality: These results concern afforestation of grassland and shrubland in paired catchments, mostly in South Africa, Australia and New Zealand, rather than restoration of degraded forest land, so the size of the loss for restoring native forest on cleared land is not measured here [ev_water_yield_farley05_1]. The row rests on one global synthesis of measured catchments and one regional expert synthesis citing earlier work [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].

forest_restoration__water_stress__income.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate water availability and the harvesting or collection of water as improved after afforestation in Cabo Verde and after afforestation of bare land in karst areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1523_2011_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_water_availability].
forest_restoration__water_stress__income.conditionality: These are compiler ratings from two technology sheets, with no comment on how the gain arises and no measured flow, soil-moisture or groundwater data; the row applies to upper-middle-income contexts only. Water leaving the catchment for downstream users is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

forest_restoration__waterlogging__all.mechanism: The Uzbekistan compiler credits afforestation of degraded irrigated cropland with strong bio-drainage through tree transpiration [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1533_2011_excess_water_drainage]. Compilers for an Ethiopian area closure and for closure with acacia reforestation in Tunisia also rate excess-water drainage as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_excess_water_drainage].
forest_restoration__waterlogging__all.conditionality: Another Ethiopian area closure is rated as slightly worsening drainage and tree planting in Uganda as leaving it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_excess_water_drainage]. All units are practitioner ratings, and only the Uzbekistan sheet states a mechanism, in an irrigated setting.

forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for broadleaf plantations with assisted tree regeneration in India and for community reforestation of microbasins in Honduras rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as decreased; the Indian compiler says erosion impacts from extreme rain storms are reduced by decreasing flow velocity, and the Honduran compiler that forests reduce the risk of landslides, with the effect greater in the long term [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all.conditionality: Both units are compiler ratings, not measurements, and neither comment concerns wind: they describe erosion and landslide risk under storm rainfall, so the row says little about shelter from cyclone winds or surge. The Honduras compiler rates only a slight reduction [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.mechanism: Compilers for mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh, a programme of broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries in India, and community reforestation of micro-basins in Honduras rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced; the India compiler attributes this to lower flow velocity reducing erosion from extreme rain storms, and the Honduras compiler to forests reducing landslide risk [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings from technology sheets, not measurements, and none describes reduced wind damage: the explained ratings work through rain-storm erosion and landslides. The Bangladesh and Honduras compilers rate only a slight reduction, the Honduras compiler expecting a greater effect in the long term [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.mechanism: Mangrove planting in northern Viet Nam is credited with protecting a sea dyke that a comparable typhoon had damaged before planting, and with cutting the share of shrimp-farm value destroyed from 90 to 25 per cent; planted mangroves in Hainan, China reduced mean wind speed behind the stand during typhoons [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. Compilers rate mangrove buffers in the Philippines as reducing cyclone impacts and afforestation in Cabo Verde and saxaul dune belts in Turkmenistan as lowering wind speed, by 20-25% in the saxaul belts [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_578_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1529_2012_wind_velocity].
forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.conditionality: The Viet Nam figures are uncontrolled before-and-after comparisons attributed to mangroves by the implementing Red Cross programme's evaluators. The Cabo Verde and Turkmenistan ratings concern everyday wind, not cyclones, and all WOCAT units are practitioner ratings.
